heading: Your security keys and smart cards
intro: Each physical key or card this service has recorded you as holding. A key is recorded only when its own attestation names its serial, so a key you registered without your organisation's enterprise attestation is not listed here; its passkey is on the Passkeys page.
none: No security key or smart card is recorded for you.
lost.what: Reporting a key lost removes its passkeys, revokes its certificates and signs out the sessions they signed in, at once. If you find it again, register it again.
done.lost: The key is reported lost, and {n} of your credentials on it were retired.
done.notAll: {n} could not be retired: ask your administrator to remove them.
done.sessionsEnded: {n} sign-on sessions it signed in were ended.
done.recovery: Your next sign-in without a passkey will ask you to register a new one before you can use any application.
done.noWayIn: It was your only way to sign in: ask your administrator for an activation link, or use your recovery codes.
claim.heading: Claim a token you were given
claim.intro: If your organisation handed you a one-time code token, type the serial printed on it and a code it shows now. It becomes your second factor.
done.claimed: Token {serial} is yours. You will be asked for one of its codes the next time you sign in.
piv.heading: Enrol a PIV certificate
piv.intro: Generate the key on your YubiKey, ask for its certificate and attest the key, then paste the three texts here. The attestation proves the key was made on the key and never left it, and only then does the certificate count as a hardware key when you sign in.
piv.commands:
ykman piv keys generate --algorithm ECCP256 --pin-policy ONCE --touch-policy ALWAYS 9a public.pem
ykman piv certificates request --subject "CN=you" 9a public.pem request.csr
ykman piv keys attest 9a attestation.pem
ykman piv certificates export f9 f9.pem
piv.fileRead: {name} is a valid PEM and was put in the box.
piv.required: This service requires the attestation for these profiles.
piv.optional: The attestation is optional; without it the certificate is issued but earns no hardware claim.
piv.noProfiles: This service issues no PIV certificate profile here. Ask your administrator.
piv.issuedWhat: Save it as cert.pem and write it to the slot with: ykman piv certificates import {slot} cert.pem
escrow.heading: Escrowed encryption keys
escrow.intro: Keys for slot 9d that this service generated and keeps sealed, so you can read old encrypted mail if your key or card is lost. An escrowed key is not a hardware key. Recovering one asks for a fresh sign-in.
escrow.none: No escrowed key is held for you.
escrow.subject: Certificate
escrow.recoveredWhat: Keep this private key as safe as the card itself. Save it as key.pem and import it with: ykman piv keys import 9d key.pem
done.enrolled: Certificate {serial} was issued from the attested key and recorded on your security key.
done.enrolledPlain: Certificate {serial} was issued. No attestation was given, so it earns no hardware claim.
done.recovered: The escrowed key of certificate {serial} was recovered.
done.attached: The escrowed certificate was noted on {key}.
tk.unavailable: This part could not be read just now. Its own page may show it.
tk.ssh.heading: Your SSH user certificates
tk.ssh.intro: Certificates this realm's SSH user certificate authority issued to you that have not expired, newest first.
tk.ssh.none: You have no SSH user certificate.
tk.ssh.issueIntro: Paste one OpenSSH public key line. A certificate lasts at most {software} seconds, or {hardware} seconds for a security key whose attestation was verified. A server that trusts this realm's SSH user CA accepts it.
tk.ssh.issuedWhat: Save it beside your public key, under the same name ending in -cert.pub. It is shown only now.
tk.ssh.pqcWhat: The post-quantum certificate issued beside it, for a server that verifies ssh-mldsa-65:
